## Summary

The mcp blue-green deploy block documents itself as INDEPENDENT of the review-bot block above
it, but it sits AFTER that block's `exit 0`. When the review-bot is busy, the deferral path
terminates the whole script, so the mcp deploy never runs. The documented independence is false
in the only case where it matters — a shared `src/rebar` change, which triggers BOTH triggers.

## The coupling, in the code

The mcp blue-green block documents itself as "INDEPENDENT of the review-bot block above", but
it sits AFTER that block's `exit 0`. When a review is in flight the drain gate defers and exits
the whole PROCESS, so the mcp block is never reached. Both trigger lists start with `src/rebar`,
so any library change matches BOTH — and the bot drains with a single worker, making
`in_flight > 0` its normal state.

## Observed impact (2026-08-26)

The review-bot drains its queue with a single worker, so `in_flight > 0` is its normal steady
state under any pipelining — in practice ~every tick deferred. Two commits merged at 06:47Z were
still not running forty minutes later, with `deploy_deferrals` at 2-3 per five-minute bucket,
unbroken. One of those commits was the mcp secrets-refresh fix, so the deploy path could not
repair itself.

## Why the alarm did not catch it

`deploy_deferrals` counts deferrals, and deferring is the CORRECT behaviour for the bot — the
alarm fires on failures, and nothing failed. The mcp deploy simply never ran.

## Proposed fix

Scope the deferral to the bot block instead of terminating the script. `autodeploy.sh` is a
linear oneshot with no enclosing loop, so `continue` is not available: HOIST the bot block into
a new function `deploy_review_bot`, and have the deferral set `bot_deferred=1` and `return 0`
from it. Control then reaches the mcp block. The mcp path is a pointer-swap that never kills an
in-flight op, so it has no reason to wait on the bot's drain. The function wrapper also keeps
indentation unchanged, so the diff stays a few hunks instead of re-indenting fifty lines.

**The tick still stops before the footer.** Letting control past the old `exit 0` must not turn
a deferred tick into a completed one, so a guard placed AFTER the mcp block and BEFORE the
footer exits when the bot deferred (or when either component was skipped with a delta still
pending). Everything the footer does is therefore skipped exactly as the `exit 0` skipped it:
`deployed-sha` and both component markers stay unadvanced, and `rm -f "$DEFER_FILE"` does not
run — the deferral EPISODE carries forward, which is what keeps `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` reachable.
Clearing it on a deferred tick would reset the bound every tick and the gate would defer
forever instead of eventually recreating the container. The ONLY behavioural difference from
the pre-fix path is that the mcp block above already ran.

Take care that the deferral episode bookkeeping (`DEFER_FILE`, `:538`) and the
`record_backoff_failure` semantics stay unchanged for the bot path, and that a bot deferral
still results in the same exit status the timer expects when the mcp block also does nothing.

## Test gap that let this through

`test_shared_src_change_triggers_both_targets` already drives a shared `src/rebar` change and
asserts both targets build — but with the bot IDLE, so it never reaches the deferral path. The
uncovered case is a shared change while the bot is BUSY, the state that made the mcp deploy
unreachable. The mcp fixture's stub also answered only `Dockerfile.mcp`; it now answers the
path list it is asked about.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A tick where the review-bot block DEFERS still reaches the mcp blue-green block, so a
      shared `src/rebar` change deploys the mcp service without waiting on the bot's drain.
- [ ] The bot path's deferral bookkeeping (episode file, bound, markers) and backoff semantics
      are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression coverage drives a tick with BOTH triggers matching and the bot busy, asserting
      the mcp container is still deployed — the case the current stub makes unreachable.
- [ ] The stub in `test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` no longer forces bot-block-false, or a new
      test supplies a git stub reporting a shared `src/rebar` change.

## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q -p no:randomly
    bash -n infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh && shellcheck -S error infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh

The new coverage has teeth when: with the `exit 0` restored in the deferral path, the new
both-triggers test FAILS (no mcp deploy), and with the scoped `return` fix it PASSES.
## Scope growth across review rounds

Four review rounds each found the same shape, each fix exposing the next: ONE piece of global
state standing in for TWO independently-deploying components.

**Completion.** `deployed-sha` is written once, at the footer, so any early exit loses the
completion of whichever component DID deploy and the next tick redeploys it — and a bot redeploy
stop-and-drains, killing an in-flight review (bug 34cd). Each component now records its own
marker the moment it completes, and — the half that makes the marker do anything — each
component's delta gate is RE-POINTED to diff from that marker instead of the global `$DEPLOYED`
baseline (`changed_range "$bot_deployed" …`, `changed_range "$mcp_deployed" …`), so a component
already at $TARGET computes no delta and is skipped. An absent or unparseable marker falls back
to `$DEPLOYED`, so the first tick after upgrade decides exactly as it does today.

**Failure.** `record_backoff_failure` wrote one `deploy-backoff` keyed on the global `$TARGET`
and the top-level gate exited the whole script on it — so an mcp failure throttled the BOT and a
bot failure suppressed mcp. Today `record_backoff_failure` is called from BOTH blocks (~5 sites
in the bot block, ~10 in the mcp block). This change re-points the mcp block's sites to a new
mcp-scoped recorder, AFTER WHICH the existing file records bot failures only — which is what
makes it safe to move its gate from the top of the script into the bot block.

**Incompleteness.** A component skipped by its own backoff window has not deployed, but nothing
said so, so the footer stamped `$TARGET` into its marker for a deploy that never ran — after
which the next tick computed no delta and dropped the change PERMANENTLY. `bot_incomplete` /
`mcp_incomplete` mark it and the footer guard honours both. Each gate tests the DELTA before the
window, keeping "nothing to do" distinct from "skipped with work pending".



## Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] A DEFERRED-bot tick deploys mcp but records NOTHING as complete: deployed-sha and
      bot-deployed-sha unadvanced, and the deferral-episode file preserved.
      Proof: `test_bot_deferral_still_reaches_the_mcp_blue_green_deploy`
- [ ] An mcp failure does not write the SHARED backoff.
      Proof: `test_mcp_failure_on_a_deferred_tick_does_not_backoff_the_bot`
- [ ] An mcp failure does not cause the bot to redeploy on later ticks.
      Proof: `test_a_failed_mcp_deploy_does_not_redeploy_the_bot_every_tick`
- [ ] A bot skipped by its backoff window is not recorded as deployed.
      Proof: `test_bot_backoff_tick_does_not_record_the_bot_as_deployed`
- [ ] An mcp skipped by its backoff window is not recorded as deployed.
      Proof: `test_mcp_backoff_tick_does_not_record_mcp_as_deployed`
- [ ] An open backoff window with NO pending delta is not reported as a skip.
      Proof: `test_an_open_bot_backoff_with_no_pending_delta_is_not_reported_as_a_skip`
- [ ] The mcp backoff window skips mcp without stopping the tick.
      Proof: `test_mcp_backoff_window_skips_the_mcp_deploy_without_stopping_the_tick`
- [ ] mcp failures still emit `deploy_failed`, tagged `component=mcp`.
      Proof: `test_mcp_failure_keeps_the_deploy_failed_metric_and_names_the_component`
